secondaryKeywords: how to verify google business profile
metaTitle: Google Business Profile, Explained for Owners
metaDescription: A Google Business Profile is your free listing in Maps and the local pack. Primary category decides more of your ranking than anything else you control.
definition: A Google Business Profile is the free business listing Google uses to place you in Maps and in the local pack results above the normal blue links.
answer: A Google Business Profile is the free listing that puts your business in Google Maps and the local pack. Google ranks those results on relevance, distance and prominence — and the biggest lever you control is your primary category, which most businesses pick carelessly in the first five minutes of signup.
takeaways: Relevance, distance and prominence. Google publishes those three factors itself; everything else you read is inference on top of them.
You get **one** primary category. It decides which searches you're eligible for at all, and it's the single most consistently cited local ranking factor among practitioners.
Postcard verification is the slow road in India. Have your signage, board and utility or GST documents ready and take the video route.
A listed address you don't actually operate from is the most common reason Indian listings get suspended — and reinstatement is a far worse week than setting it up correctly.

sections.h2: The three factors Google says it ranks on
body: Google publishes its local ranking logic in plain language, which is unusually generous of it. **Relevance** — how well your profile matches what someone searched. **Distance** — how far you are from the searcher or the place they named. **Prominence** — how well known the business is, drawn from links, articles, directories and reviews.

Distance you can't change without moving. Prominence is slow, and mostly a by-product of your off-page work. Relevance responds this week — decided by your categories, business name, services list and description.

sections.h2: Primary category is the decision that carries the weight
body: Google offers a few thousand categories, you pick one primary, and you can add secondaries. Practitioners surveyed year after year for Whitespark's Local Search Ranking Factors put primary category at or near the top of the local pack list, and you can verify it yourself in any Indian city in ten minutes.

The reason is mechanical. Google maps a query to an implied category, then filters the candidate set. "Marketing agency", "Advertising agency", "Internet marketing service" and "Website designer" are four different filters. Pick the wrong one and no amount of review generation or [local citation](/glossary/local-citations) work makes you eligible for the search you want.

The method is free. Search your money query in Maps, on a phone, from the area you serve. Open the top three profiles and read the category under each business name. If one dominates and it's honestly accurate for you, that's your primary. Secondaries widen eligibility at less weight — add the ones you genuinely deliver, then stop.

callout.title: Change it once, and write down the date
callout.body: Changing the primary category on an established listing can move rankings within days, either direction. Change one thing, note the date, wait two weeks. Businesses that rewrite category, name and description in one afternoon learn nothing from the result.

sections.h2: Verification, and why Indian listings stall here
body: You can't rank an unverified profile, and verification is where most Indian setups lose a month. Google leans heavily on video verification now: one unbroken recording tying your signage to your street, your street to your interior, and finally showing you accessing something only staff could — a till, a back office, a locked cabinet.
Postcards still exist and they're the slow road. Complexes, gated societies, shared offices and unnumbered lanes defeat them regularly, and a failure costs you the wait plus a re-request.
bullets: **Before you film:** put up permanent signage. A printed sheet taped to a glass door reads as temporary and gets rejected.
**Film continuously.** Stopping and restarting is the most common rejection reason — Google needs one shot proving the pieces are the same place.
**Keep documents ready:** GST certificate, Shops and Establishments registration, a utility bill in the business name.
**Coworking desks and virtual offices** rarely survive review — every business at that address competes to be the one Google keeps.

sections.h2: Reviews: the count, the pace and the replies
body: Reviews do two jobs and only one of them is ranking. They feed prominence, and they close the sale on the profile itself — plenty of local buyers never reach your website at all, which is the argument in [Google Business Profile vs a website](/compare/google-business-profile-vs-website).

Three things matter more than a perfect score. **Count relative to the profiles you're competing with in the same pack**, not an absolute target. **Pace**, because forty reviews in a week after two silent years reads as exactly what it is. And **replies**, which Google explicitly asks for and which are the only part of the section you control.

A five-star average with eleven reviews loses to a 4.6 with 340. Perfect scores also depress conversion — buyers read the bad ones first, and a calm, specific reply does more for you than the review costs.

callout.title: Don't buy them, and don't trade them
callout.body: Bought reviews get filtered, removed, and can take the listing with them. Offering a discount for a review breaks Google's policy too, however normal that has become in Indian retail. Ask every customer, immediately, with a short link. That's the entire legal playbook.

sections.h2: Address or service area — pick the one that's true
body: If customers come to you, show the address. If you go to them — plumbers, packers, photographers, most agencies — hide the address and set service areas instead. A hidden address with service areas is a fully supported configuration, not a downgrade.

Set service areas as towns or regions rather than dozens of pincodes; the list is capped and a sprawling one doesn't buy extra reach. And accept the trade-off honestly: service-area businesses are still ranked from their registered address, so a Whitefield business doesn't compete evenly in Jayanagar however wide the area is drawn.

The temptation is to list a friend's shop, a relative's flat or a virtual office in the suburb you want. That's the most common reason listings get suspended, and reinstatement means producing the documents you didn't have in the first place. If you need real presence across the city, that's a second premises, not a second listing. [Local SEO work](/services/local-seo-services) can do a lot; it can't relocate you.

faqs.q: Is Google Business Profile the same as Google My Business?
faqs.a: Yes — Google renamed Google My Business to Google Business Profile and moved management into Search and Maps directly. The old standalone app is gone. If a proposal still says "GMB listing setup", that's a decent clue about when the deck was last updated.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right primary category?
faqs.a: Search your money query in Maps from the area you serve, open the top three ranking profiles, and read the category under each business name. If one dominates and it's genuinely accurate for you, use it as your primary. Add secondaries only for services you actually deliver.

faqs.q: How long does Google Business Profile verification take in India?
faqs.a: Video verification is usually reviewed within a few days. Postcards are the slow route and frequently fail outright at complexes, gated societies and shared buildings. Have permanent signage, a continuous video, and your GST or Shops and Establishments paperwork ready before you start.

faqs.q: How many reviews do I need to rank in the local pack?
faqs.a: There's no number — it's relative. Look at the review counts of the three profiles currently ranking for your query and treat that as the field. Steady, ongoing reviews from real customers beat a burst, and replying to all of them matters more than protecting a five-star average.

faqs.q: Can I rank in a city I don't have an address in?
faqs.a: Not reliably. Distance is one of Google's three stated factors and it's measured from your verified location. Service areas broaden who you appear for, not where you're measured from. Listing an address you don't operate from is the fastest route to a suspended profile.

faqs.q: Do Google Business Profile posts affect rankings?
faqs.a: There's no strong evidence they move local pack position. They do occupy space on your profile, answer questions before someone calls, and show recent activity to a human reading you. Treat posts as conversion work, not ranking work, and don't let anyone bill them as a growth lever.
